title: Torchbearer shift brief — 2026-11-05
content:
Shift summary:

Owner: Aisha Patel (torchbearer) — handoff to Diego Ramos at 08:00 UTC
Shift window: 00:00–08:00 PT (overnight NA / EU overlap)
Primary focus: steady-state latency, KV/prefix cache churn after 03:10 UTC, verify Dedicated pool fallback health

What happened (timeline highlights):
- 02:58 UTC — Spike in token-generation P95 (from 230ms -> 980ms) on hosted-api-prod. Alert: latency-token-p95-high across eu-west-1.
- 03:05 UTC — KV cache eviction storm observed on ranger-serve-*. Metrics: cache-eviction-rate x6 baseline; mem-usage per pod dropped then recovered.
- 03:12 UTC — Smart routing kicked fallback for 6% of requests to model-xx-quantized due to capacity pressure. No customer-facing errors observed.
- 03:22 UTC — Dedicated pool gpu-sat alert triggered for pool-dedicated-02 (GPU util 98%). Autoscaler added 1 node; observed longer queue depth for ~90s.
- 04:10 UTC — On-call manually cycled ranger-cache-controller on nodes a,b to flush stuck state (see commands below). After restart P95 returned to ~270ms by 04:30 UTC.

What we did:
- Followed runbook: 'latency-spike-detection-v2' to narrow to KV cache churn and eviction latencies.
- Restarted ranger-cache-controller pods (kubectl rollout restart deployment/ranger-cache-controller -n infra).
- Increased cache-ttl for prefix-cache from 300s -> 900s as temporary mitigation (configmap infra/cache-config v2 -> v2b).
- Opened OPS ticket JIRA-OPS-9821 for postmortem and capacity review.
- Notified product/SRE owners in #sre-ops and #prod-telemetry.

Outstanding items / follow-ups (owners assigned):
- Diego Ramos: schedule deeper heap / pprof analysis against ranger-serve at 03:05 window; attach artifacts to JIRA-OPS-9821. (due 2026-11-07)
- Marta Chen: verify autoscaler policy for dedicated pools — investigate why scale-up took ~60–120s instead of target 30s. Possible policy tweak: pre-provision buffer for burst mode. (due 2026-11-09)
- Liam O'Connor: add observability probe that captures KV eviction rate and cache miss ratio in a single dashboard panel for quick triage. (due 2026-11-06)
- Aisha (me): draft runbook update for 'cache-eviction-storms' section with explicit rollback steps for cache-ttl change and a small playbook for manual rotor restarts. (draft attached: CONFLUENCE-Runbooks-CacheEviction)

Runbook draft notes (things to include / clarify):
- Detection: define dual-threshold (P95 > 400ms AND cache-eviction-rate > 3x baseline for 5m) before invoking manual mitigation. Reduce false positives when traffic bursts occur.
- Mitigation order (short form):
  1) Check autoscaler and pool saturation (kubectl top / cloud console);
  2) Confirm eviction storm (metrics -> infra.cache.evictions per pod);
  3) If eviction storm confirmed and eviction latency > 150ms: increase cache-ttl on canary config (prefix-cache) and apply to 1 node;
  4) If no improvement in 5m: restart ranger-cache-controller pods on affected nodes (kubectl rollout restart);
  5) If still no improvement: route 5–10% traffic to model-xx-quantized fallback and file incident escalation to infra-lead.

Technical commands & logs used during triage: (copy/paste safe)
- kubectl --context=prod get pods -n infra -l app=ranger-cache-controller -o wide
- kubectl --context=prod logs deploy/ranger-cache-controller -n infra --since=30m | grep eviction
- curl -s http://metrics.internal/api/query?metric=infra.cache.evictions&window=15m | jq '.'
- applied configmap patch: kubectl -n infra patch configmap cache-config --patch '{"data":{"prefix_cache_ttl":"900"}}'

Metrics snapshot at peak (03:10 UTC):
- token-generation P95: 980ms (baseline 230ms)
- infra.cache.evictions per pod per min: 62 (baseline 10)
- GPU util (pool-dedicated-02): 98% -> steadied to 62% after scale-up
- errors 5xx rate: small bump 0.02% -> 0.14% (no major customer impact)

Alerts fired (list):
- latency-token-p95-high (acknowledged)
- infra.cache.eviction-spike (acknowledged)
- dedicated-pool-gpu-sat (auto-resolved after scale)

Customer impact:
- No customer-facing errors observed; small increase in tail latency for interactive customers in eu-west-1 for ~40–70 seconds. No support tickets opened during window.

Proposed longer-term actions (backlog / not immediate):
- Evaluate smarter eviction algorithm (LRU -> frequency-weighted) for prefix cache; prototype in staging. (Research owner: Marta)
- Add canary throttle to autoscaler triggers to reduce reaction time under short intense bursts. (owner: Platform Eng)
- Add a post-incident synthetic test that simulates cache-eviction storm and verifies routing/fallback behavior. (owner: DevEx)

Notes to next on-call (Diego):
- If you see P95 creep again: start at the runbook detection step above. Don’t increase TTL above 1800s cluster-wide without approval — causes memory pressure on edge nodes.
- Check PR #451 in infra repo — I pushed a small config patch for TTL change (reverted after window). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/451
- Ticket: JIRA-OPS-9821 contains logs + links to snapshots. I'll add heap dumps once Diego confirms retrieval completed.

Questions / unresolved:
- Why eviction rate spiked on a subset of ranger-serve pods instead of uniformly — possible hot key / uneven traffic routing? Need request trace sampling to correlate.
- Was there any coincident job (cron) running in eu-west that could have warmed caches or triggered eviction? Confirm with infra-scheduler logs.

Quick contacts (for escalation):
- Marta Chen (platform): @marta (slack), +1-415-555-0172
- Samir Gupta (runtime): @samirg (slack)
- On-call infra-lead (rotation): paged via ops-pager if incident > sev2

Misc / scratch:
- I left rough pprof commands in the JIRA ticket.
- Consider adding eviction-rate alert noise suppression tied to traffic-window percentiles.
- If you have time, Diego, snapshot the tracer spans for 03:00–03:30 to see long-tail calls to kv-store (trace IDs -> attached).

End of shift: handoff to Diego at 08:00 UTC.

— Aisha
